chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) accepted the testimony of one man and the oath of the creditor in debt cases, but he did not accept anything less than two just witnesses for the new moon (of Ramadan).

key_terms.الْهِلَال: The new moon (specifically referring to the sighting for Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: What are the different requirements for witnesses in debt cases versus lunar month sighting in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s pragmatic approach to evidence, distinguishing between financial transactions and religious observances. While debt disputes allow for a single witness combined with the creditor's oath (*yamin*), the sighting of the lunar month (*Hilal*) strictly requires two just witnesses (*shahiday 'adl*), underscoring the communal certainty needed for determining Islamic calendar events like Ramadan. This distinction reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing individual testimony with public verification in matters of worship.
